data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Otho meaning 'wealthy' and the suffix -ilia meaning 'battle' or 'fertility'. In Greek mythology, Othilia was a warrior goddess associated with fertility and abundance. In Christian tradition, Othilia is revered as a saint who miraculously gave birth after a long period of infertility. The name Othilia carries the meaning “Fertile in battle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Othilia usually hope their child will grow to embody fertile in battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
